```{=html}
    <span class="variant-id">VAR_SHBMV01P155A</span> <span class="variant-id">VAR_STBXV05P244A</span> <span class="variant-id">VAR_TDAHV01P088C</span> أخبرنا عبد الواحد بن أحمد المليحي أنا أبو منصور محمد بن محمد بن سمعان نا أبو جعفر محمد بن أحمد بن عبد الجبار الرياني نا حميد بن زنجويه نا يعلى بن عبيد نا محمد بن إسحاق عن محمد بن إبراهيم عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن زيد بن خالد الجهني رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لولا أن أشق على أمتي لأخرت العشاء إلى ثلث الليل ولأمرتهم بالسواك عند كل صلاة. <span class="page-no" title="end of page 393 of vol. 1">§</span>
  </div>
</article>


<article class="sira-report sira-variant-card" id="TDAHV01P088C" lang="ar" dir="rtl">

  <div class="witness-text">
    <span class="variant-id">VAR_SHBMV01P155A</span> <span class="variant-id">VAR_STBXV05P244A</span> <span class="variant-id">VAR_HMBSV01P393B</span> أخبرنا القاضي أبو الخير سعادة بن إبراهيم بن أحمد بن بكران الخسويى الأديب نجدي بقراءتي عليه في داره في جمادى الأولى سنة تسع وعشرين وخمسمائة أيضا قال أبو محمد عبد الله بن احمد بن حرير السلماسي بها قال أنبا أبو مسعود أحمد بن محمد البجلي أنبا أبو النضر محمد بن احمد سليمان الشرمعدلي بها ح وأخبرنا به عاليا أبو عبد الله محمد بن الفضل الفراوي بنيسابور أنبأ الشريف أبو بكر محمد بن عبد الله بن عمر العمري الهروي أنبا أبو محمد عبد الرحمن بن أحمد بن أبي شريح الأنصاري قالا أنبا أبو جعفر محمد بن أحمد بن عبد الجبار ثنا أبو أحمد حميد بن <span class="page-no" title="end of page 88 of vol. 1">§</span> زانجويه ثنا يعلى بن عبيد ثنا محمد بن إسحاق عن محمد بن إبراهيم عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن زيد بن خالد الجهني رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لولا أن أشق على أمتي لأخرت صلاه العشاء إلى ثلث الليل ولأمرتهم بالسواك عند كل صلاة فكان زيد بن خالد سواكه على أذنه بموضع القلم من أذن الكاتب لا يقوم لصلاة إلا استن ثم رده لموضعه ثالثا درجة الحديث ومن اخرجه <span class="page-no" title="end of page 89 of vol. 1">§</span>
  </div>
</article>

</div>
```

```{=html}
  </div>
</article>
```

```{=html}
<article class="sira-report" id="NSSXV01P162A" lang="ar" dir="rtl">
  <header class="sira-report-header" lang="en" dir="ltr">

  </header>
  <div class="witness-text">
    وحدثني علي بن عيسى واللفظ له ثنا مسدد بن قطن ثنا عثمان بن أبي شيبة ثنا يعلى بن عبيد ثنا محمد بن إسحاق عن الزهري عن محمد بن جبير بن مطعم عن أبيه قال قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالخيف من منى فقال نضر الله عبدا سمع مقالتي فوعاها ثم أداها إلى من لم يسمعها فرب حامل فقه لا فقه له ورب حامل فقه إلى من هوأفقه منه ثلاث لا يغل عليهن قلب مؤمن إخلاص العمل لله والنصيحة لأولي الأمر ولزوم الجماعة فإن دعوتهم تكون من ورائهم قد اتفق هؤلاء الثقات على رواية هذا الحديث عن محمد بن إسحاق عن الزهري وخالفهم عبد الله بن نمير وحده فقال عن محمد بن إسحاق عن عبد السلام وهو ابن أبي الجنوب عن الزهري وابن نمير ثقة والله أعلم ثم نظرناه فوجدنا للزهري فيه متابعا عن محمد بن جبير. <span class="page-no" title="end of page 162 of vol. 1">§</span>
  </div>
</article>
```
```{=html}
<article class="sira-report" id="NSSXV01P413A" lang="ar" dir="rtl">

  </header>
  <div class="witness-text">
    أخبرنا أبو جعفر محمد بن علي الشيباني بالكوفة ثنا أحمد بن حازم الغفاري ثنا يعلى بن عبيد ثنا محمد بن إسحاق عن محمد بن إبراهيم بن الحارث التيمي عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن أبي هريرة قال جئت الطور فلقيت هناك كعب الأحبار فحدثته عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وحدث عن التوراة فما اختلفا حتى مررت بيوم الجمعة قال قلت قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في كل يوم جمعة ساعة لا يوافقها مؤمن وهو يصلي يسأل الله شيئا إلا أعطاه إياه قال كعب تلك في كل سنة فقلت ما كذلك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرجع فتلا ثم قال صدق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في كل جمعة قال أبو هريرة ثم لقيت عبد الله بن سلام فحدثته بمجلسي مع كعب. <span class="page-no" title="end of page 413 of vol. 1">§</span>
```

[^comment-IBABV01P081B-1]: <a href="../references.html#ref-HHMX" class="source-ref">HHMXV07P379A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Razzāq b. Hammām al-Ḥumayrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muṣannaf</span>, vol. 7 p. 379) places this in the context of Ibn al-Nuʿmān and <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV03P375A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 375) quotes a portion of the passage in the biography of al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr (although he appears to suggest that Ibn Isḥāq names him as al-Nuʿaymān). <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV03P375A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 375) states that Nuʿaymān b. ʿAmr was the younger brother of Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr. Ibn al-Nuʿaymān or al-Nuʿaymān is not mentioned in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. He is sometimes identified as al-Nuʿaymān b. ʿAmr b. Rifāʿah b. al-Ḥārith. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-JWZX" class="source-ref">JWZXV05P277A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Jawzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muntaẓam fī Tārīkh al-mulūk waʾl-umam</span>, vol. 5 p. 277), al-Nuʿaymān participated in Badr, and all of the famous battles in which Muḥammad fought. He was known to have repeatedly been punished for drinking nabīdh. <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV06P431A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 6 p. 431) and <a href="../references.html#ref-TBRC" class="source-ref">TBRCV11P554A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-rusul waʾl-mulūk</span>, vol. 11 p. 554) mention the account of ʿUqbah b. al-Ḥārith where he describes being ordered by Muḥammad to beat Ibn Nuʿaymān or al-Nuʿaymān with shoes and palm branches for drinking. <a href="../references.html#ref-TKXX" class="source-ref">TKXXV03P375A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Saʿd</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 375) states he died in during the caliphate of Muʿawīyah but <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHB" class="source-ref">KTHBV08P070A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bidāyat waʾl-nihāyah</span>, vol. 8 p. 70) places his death in the year 54. <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRS" class="source-ref">HJRSV06P353A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Iṣābah fī tamyīz al-ṣaḥābah</span>, vol. 6 p. 353) states that Ibn Isḥāq identifies him as al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr and not as al-Nuʿaymān, this follows the comment of Ibn Hishām in vol. 1, 703A. A person identified as al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr is mention twice in the redaction of Ibn Hishām: on vol. 1, 552A he is identified as a Jew who was one of two Rabbis who questioned Muḥammad and then rejected him. On vol. 1, 703A he is identified as al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr b. Rifāʿah b. Sawād, a member of the Sawād b. Mālik b. Ghamm clan, among the Anṣ ār, who participated at Badr. Ibn Hishām, in his commentary, states his name was Nuʿaymān. It is not clear if Ibn Isḥāq understood al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAmr to be the individual who is commonly referred to as being punished for drinking. For passages within the Ibn Isḥāq tradition that identify Nuʿaymān or al-Nuʿaymān with the subject of the person punished for drinking, see via <a href="WSASN.html" class="witness-link">WSASN</a> (Sharīk b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Sharīk al-Najaʿī al-Kūfī): <a href="../references.html#ref-NSKX" class="source-ref">NSKXV05P143B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Nasāʾī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 5 p. 143) and <a href="../references.html#ref-IHMA" class="source-ref">IHMAV12P370B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥāzim</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muḥallā bil-Āthār</span>, vol. 12 p. 370); via the witness of <a href="WZATB.html" class="witness-link">WZATB</a> (Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ṭufayl al-Kūfī al-Bakkāʾī al-ʿĀmirī) (but not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām) <a href="../references.html#ref-NSSX" class="source-ref">NSSXV04P415A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥākim al-Nīsābūrī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Mustadrak ʿalā al-ṣaḥīḥīn</span>, vol. 4 p. 415),<a href="../references.html#ref-IHMA" class="source-ref">IHMAV12P370C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥāzim</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muḥallā bil-Āthār</span>, vol. 12 p. 370), <a href="../references.html#ref-BQRX" class="source-ref">BQRXV03P340B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sunan al-ṣaghīr</span>, vol. 3 p. 340), <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV08P545B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 8 p. 545), and <a href="../references.html#ref-BQMX" class="source-ref">BQMXV13P039A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Maʿrifat al-sunan waʾl-āthār</span>, vol. 13 p. 39); via the witness of <a href="WYUAU.html" class="witness-link">WYUAU</a> (Yaʿlā b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah al-Īyādī al-Tanāfisī al-Kūfī), <a href="../references.html#ref-IBAB" class="source-ref">IBABV01P081B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Bishrān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Amālī Ibn Bishrān</span>, vol. 1 p. 81), <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV08P545A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 8 p. 545), and <a href="../references.html#ref-KHTS" class="source-ref">KHTSV04P307A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Ismāʾ al-mubhamah fī al-anbāʾ al-muḥkamah</span>, vol. 4 p. 307); via <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī): <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV32P210A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 32 p. 210); and via <a href="WHSSH.html" class="witness-link">WHSSH</a> (WHSSH): <a href="../references.html#ref-KHTS" class="source-ref">KHTSV04P307B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Ismāʾ al-mubhamah fī al-anbāʾ al-muḥkamah</span>, vol. 4 p. 307) and <a href="../references.html#ref-YNBH" class="source-ref">YNBHV12P358D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-ʿAynī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bināyah sharḥ al-Hidāyah</span>, vol. 12 p. 358). Without a witness, <a href="../references.html#ref-YNBH" class="source-ref">YNBHV12P358A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-ʿAynī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bināyah sharḥ al-Hidāyah</span>, vol. 12 p. 358).
[^comment-SMJXV01P535F-1]: This is part of a series of traditions that appear to originate with Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd that discuss vomiting and its impact on the status of fasting. In this series there is a great deal of variation, but most suggest that Faḍālah was with the prophet and when someone offered him a drink or when he asked for a drink, Muḥammad was asked about the status of his fast. He replies generally that he was had been fasting but then vomited and was no longer fasting. In some traditions in the series there are comments about whether vomiting “breaks” the fast or if Muḥammad chose to end his fast after vomiting. There appears to be some dispute in the legal tradition about vomiting and its impact on the status of the fast, which these traditions address. The fragments are not separated into specific style types and are simply group by subject. They are witnessed by <a href="WHSDB.html" class="witness-link">WHSDB</a> (Ḥammād b. Salamah b. Dīnār al-Baṣrī): <a href="../references.html#ref-THSH" class="source-ref">THSHV04P379A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. [^comment-SHBMV01P155A-1]: Ibn Abī Shaybah goes on to say: قال فكان زيد بن خالد سواكه على أذنه موضع القلم من أذن الكاتب فلا يقوم لصلاة إلا استن ثم رده في موضعه. These specific passages are not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Placement based on content and the beginning of ritual practices, in this instance, treating the issue of ablutions for every prayer and its abrogation (approximate to <a href="../references.html#ref-HSNX" class="source-ref">HSNXV01P584D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>ʿAbd al-Malik b. Hishām</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Sīrah al-Nabuwīyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 584)). Of this tradition, Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. Sawrah al-Tirmidhī states: وقد روى هذا الحديث محمد بن إسحاق عن محمد بن إبراهيم عن أبي سلمة عن زيد بن خالد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحديث أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة وزيد بن خالد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كلاهما عندي صحيح لأنه قد روي من غير وجه عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هذا الحديث وحديث أبي هريرة إنما صح لأنه قد روي من غير وجه وأما محمد فزعم أن حديث أبي سلمة عن زيد بن خالد أصح وفي الباب عن أبي بكر الصديق وعلي وعائشة وابن عباس وحذيفة وزيد بن خالد وأنس وعبد الله بن عمرو وابن عمر وأم حبيبة وأبي أمامة وأبي أيوب وتمام بن عباس، وعبد الله بن حنظلة وأم سلمة وواثلة وأبي موسى (see <a href="../references.html#ref-TMSX" class="source-ref">TMSXV01P034B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Tirmidhī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-Tirmidhī</span>, vol. 1 p. 34)). This passage is one of the most frequently related traditions in the Ibn Isḥāq corpus with 88 witnessed variations across 13 witnesses. The largest collection of variations are in <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Yūsuf b. Muḥammad al-Zaylaʿī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Nasb al-rāyah li-aḥādīth al-hidāyah</span>, vol. 1 p. 247), <a href="../references.html#ref-IMBT" class="source-ref">IMBTV01P719A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Mulaqin</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Badr al-munīr fī takhrīj al-ahādīth waʾl-āthār al-wāqiʿah fī al-sharḥ al-kabīr</span>, vol. 1 p. 719), <a href="../references.html#ref-IMBT" class="source-ref">IMBTV02P067A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Mulaqin</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Badr al-munīr fī takhrīj al-ahādīth waʾl-āthār al-wāqiʿah fī al-sharḥ al-kabīr</span>, vol. 2 p. 67), <a href="../references.html#ref-IMTM" class="source-ref">IMTMV01P081A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn al-Mulaqin</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tadhlirat al-muḥtāj ilā aḥādīth al-minhāj</span>, vol. 1 p. 81), <a href="../references.html#ref-HYMZ" class="source-ref">HYMZV02P097A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī b. Abī Bakr Haythamī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Majmaʿ al-zawāʾid wa-manbaʿ al-fawāʾid</span>, vol. 2 p. 97), and <a href="../references.html#ref-HYMZ" class="source-ref">HYMZV10P154B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī b. Abī Bakr Haythamī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Majmaʿ al-zawāʾid wa-manbaʿ al-fawāʾid</span>, vol. 10 p. 154)). The tradition is related to Ibn Isḥāq from several different sources: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. al-Ḥārith al-Taymī, Saʿīd b. Abī Saʿīd al-Maqrubī, Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā b. Hibbān (sometimes listed as Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā b. Hissān), Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. Abī al-Rajāl al-Ṣalaḥī, and Ibn Isḥāq’s uncle, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Yasār.
[^comment-RHWXV05P127A-1]: Passage not found in HSNX. Deals with the issue of the loss of a women&#x27;s hair and according to <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRQ" class="source-ref">HJRQV05P077A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taghlīq al-taʿlīq ʿalā Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī</span>, vol. 5 p. 77), as witnessed by <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī),, in the context of the revelation of Qurʾān 24:31. <a href="../references.html#ref-HJRQ" class="source-ref">HJRQV05P077A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taghlīq al-taʿlīq ʿalā Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī</span>, vol. 5 p. 77) appears to be the only Ibn Isḥāq passage that specifically discusses this verse. That it is found in Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī seems odd given the late date of the author. Similar passage also found in <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī), <a href="WMSAH.html" class="witness-link">WMSAH</a> (Muḥammad b. Salamah b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bāhilī al-Ḥarrānī), <a href="WJHZA.html" class="witness-link">WJHZA</a> (Jarīr b. Ḥāzim b. Zayd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Shajāʿ al-Azdī al-ʿAtkī al-Baṣrī), and <a href="WASKA.html" class="witness-link">WASKA</a> (ʿAbdah (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān) b. Sulaymān al-Kilābī al-Kūfī) but do not refer to the same back story or refer to any Qurʾānic verse as a foundation. <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) and <a href="WMSAH.html" class="witness-link">WMSAH</a> (Muḥammad b. Salamah b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bāhilī al-Ḥarrānī) gives the witness as ʿĀʾishah not Asmā bint Abī Bakr.
[^comment-SHBMV03P024L-1]: This passage is not found in the redaction of Ibn Hishām. Variations of this fragment are located in <a href="WYUAU.html" class="witness-link">WYUAU</a> (Yaʿlā b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah al-Īyādī al-Tanāfisī al-Kūfī): <a href="../references.html#ref-SHBM" class="source-ref">SHBMV03P024L</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Shaybah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kitāb al-muṣannaf fī al-aḥāddīth waʾl-āthār</span>, vol. 3 p. 24); <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī): <a href="../references.html#ref-STBX" class="source-ref">STBXV18P313C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Ṭabarānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Muʿjam al-kabīr</span>, vol. 18 p. 313) and <a href="../references.html#ref-BQSX" class="source-ref">BQSXV03P576E</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Bayhaqī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sunan al-kubrā</span>, vol. 3 p. 576); <a href="WABAB.html" class="witness-link">WABAB</a> (ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Shāmī al-Baṣrī): <a href="../references.html#ref-THSH" class="source-ref">THSHV08P320A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Ṭaḥāwī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Sharḥ mushkil al-āthār</span>, vol. 8 p. 320) and <a href="../references.html#ref-SHBM" class="source-ref">SHBMV03P028G</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Shaybah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kitāb al-muṣannaf fī al-aḥāddīth waʾl-āthār</span>, vol. 3 p. 28); <a href="WMUTK.html" class="witness-link">WMUTK</a> (Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Īyādī al-Ṭanāfisī al-Kūfī): <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV39P359B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 39 p. 359); and <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī): <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV39P362A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 39 p. 362) and <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHR" class="source-ref">KTHRV07P018B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Jāmiʿ al-masānīd waʾl-sunan</span>, vol. 7 p. 18). It is a part of a series of traditions that originate from Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd, related to Ibn Isḥāq through Thumāmah b. Shufayy. According to <a href="../references.html#ref-BKHB" class="source-ref">BKHBV02P177D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh al-kabīr</span>, vol. 2 p. 177), Abū ʿAlī Thumāmah b. Shufayy al-Hamdānī only related from a few people, including Faḍālah, ʿUqbah b. ʿĀmir, and Qubayṣah b. Dhuʾayb. He appears to have been regarded as one of the people of Egypt. <a href="../references.html#ref-RZJX" class="source-ref">RZJXV02P466C</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Jarḥ waʾl-taʿdīl</span>, vol. 2 p. 466) states that Thumāmah related material to Ibn Isḥāq as well as Yazīd b. Abī Ḥabīb, the source of the only clarification tradition in the group found on in the <a href="WAKMW.html" class="witness-link">WAKMW</a> (Aḥmad b. Khālid b. Mūsā al-Wahbī al-Kindī) witness; all other the other traditions come to Ibn Isḥāq directly through Thumāmah. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Aḥmad b. Yūnus al-Ṣadafī, in his history of Egypt, refers to him as Thumāmah b. Shufayy al-Hamdānī, as well as al-Uḥrūjī al-Miṣrī, although what “Uḥrūj” refers to in not known. al-Ṣadafī claims that Thumāmah participated in the raid on Rhodes (Rūdas) with Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd and that he died before 120/737 during the caliphate of Hishām b. ʿAbd al-Mālik (reign c. 724-743) (see <a href="../references.html#ref-TYNX" class="source-ref">TYNXV01P080A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Aḥmad b. Yūnus al-Ṣadafī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Ibn Yūnus al-Miṣrī</span>, vol. 1 p. 80)). al-Mizzī states that Thumāmah settled in Alexandria (<a href="../references.html#ref-MZTX" class="source-ref">MZTXV04P404A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Mizzī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Tahdhīb al-kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 4 p. 404)). The tradition witnessed by <a href="WYUAU.html" class="witness-link">WYUAU</a> (Yaʿlā b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah al-Īyādī al-Tanāfisī al-Kūfī) and <a href="WMUTK.html" class="witness-link">WMUTK</a> (Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd b. Abī Umayyah ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Īyādī al-Ṭanāfisī al-Kūfī) (who were brothers and likely heard the story at the same time), state that the event took place in the time of Muʿāwiyah during the invasion of “Rūm” (see <a href="../references.html#ref-SHBM" class="source-ref">SHBMV03P024L</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Abī Shaybah</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kitāb al-muṣannaf fī al-aḥāddīth waʾl-āthār</span>, vol. 3 p. 24) and <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV39P359B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 39 p. 359) respectively). <a href="WSACD.html" class="witness-link">WSACD</a> (Ibrāhīm b. Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madinī al-Zuhrī) also states in one of the traditions he witnessed that it occurred during the invasion of “Rūm” but does not place it in a time period (see <a href="../references.html#ref-HBHX" class="source-ref">HBHXV39P362A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Musnad</span>, vol. 39 p. 362)). According to Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ, the invasion of Rhodes occurred in 59/678-679, the last year of Muʿāwīyah’s reign, under the leadership of Junādah b. Abī Umayyah (see <a href="../references.html#ref-SFTX" class="source-ref">SFTXV01P227B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Khalīfah b. Khayyāṭ al-Shaybānī al-ʿAṣfarī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh</span>, vol. 1 p. 227)). There is, however, some dispute about the year that Faḍālah b. ʿUbayd died, some placing his death in 53, others in 67. Ibn Kathīr, quoting Ibn al-Jawzī, states that Faḍālah died in 55, apparently just before the capture of Rhodes, which he covers in the following section (see <a href="../references.html#ref-KTHB" class="source-ref">KTHBV08P078B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Kathīr</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Bidāyat waʾl-nihāyah</span>, vol. 8 p. 78)). If this is accurate, the tradition may have had a foreshadowing element since it talks about death and burial just before Faḍālah’s own death. Placement should be in the year 55 or 56 under the heading of the Invasion of Rhodes.
